title: CORE: Uniform exponential integrability sup_N E_μ[F_N^{1+δ}] < ∞ (unbounded cubic in the exponent)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Step D — the crux.** Let $F_N=\frac{dT_\psi^*\mu_N}{d\mu_N}=e^{X_N}$ with $X_N=\langle\psi,u\rangle_H^\sim-\tfrac12\|\psi\|_H^2-[V_N(u)-V_N(u-\psi)]$. To conclude $T_\psi^*\mu\ll\mu$ with $\mathbb{E}_\mu F_\psi=1$, one needs $F_N\to F_\psi$ in $L^1(\mu)$, for which it suffices to show $\sup_N\mathbb{E}_\mu[F_N^{1+\delta}]<\infty$ for some $\delta>0$.

**Gap:** The exponent $X_N$ contains $-\int\psi\,{:}u^3{:}$, a cubic that is **unbounded below**, so direct exponential-moment bounds diverge. Provide a genuine argument, e.g.:
- the **Boué–Dupuis variational representation** of $\log\mathbb{E}_\mu e^{(1+\delta)X_N}$ as a stochastic control problem, with the cubic term absorbed by the drift energy using $\|\psi\|_{C^k}<\infty$; or
- a Nelson/hypercontractivity argument adapted to $\Phi^4_3$.

**Why very hard:** this is research-level. It is the single estimate that makes absolute continuity work; everything else is bookkeeping by comparison. Reference: Barashkov–Gubinelli, *A variational method for $\Phi^4_3$*, Duke 2020.

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**[Re: the current `solution.tex`, which proves the *equivalence* direction]**

The current attempt's uniform-integrability step (its §5.2 "Proof of (A)") is not merely unproven — **as written it is provably false**, which sharpens this CORE issue.

It claims, for $Q_\epsilon$ a finite combination of integrals of Wick powers of order $\le 3$ against smooth functions, that
$$\int e^{s Q_\epsilon}\,d\nu \le C(s,M) < \infty \quad\text{for every } s>0,$$
justified by a chaos tail $\nu(|Q_\epsilon|>t)\le 2e^{-c(t/\|Q_\epsilon\|_2)^{2/3}}$ with the parenthetical "the $t^{2/3}$ dominates the linear $st$ for large $t$."

**Disproof.**
1. $t^{2/3}\ll t$, so $st$ dominates $ct^{2/3}$ and $\int e^{st-ct^{2/3}}\,dt=+\infty$. The parenthetical is backwards.
2. Directly: a third-chaos variable $H_3(g)=g^3-3g$, $g\sim N(0,1)$, has $\mathbb E[e^{sX}]=+\infty$ for **every** $s\neq0$ (the cube blows $e^{sX}$ up on one tail); even $H_2(g)=g^2-1$ has $\mathbb E[e^{s(g^2-1)}]=\infty$ for $s\ge 1/2$. (Verified numerically.)

Hence the cubic part of $Q_\epsilon$ has $\int e^{sQ_\epsilon}d\nu=+\infty$ for all $s\neq0$, and the Hölder-against-(P4) route to $\sup_\epsilon\int G_\epsilon^q\,d\mu_\epsilon<\infty$ collapses for the cubic exponent.

**Conclusion / fix.** A correct integrability input cannot come from GFF chaos exponential moments. It must be a $\mu$-adapted bound: Hairer–Steele sub-Gaussian tails for $\mu$, or the Boué–Dupuis variational representation of $\log\mathbb E_\mu e^{(1+\delta)X_N}$ as a stochastic-control problem with the unbounded-below cubic absorbed by the drift energy (using $\|\psi\|_{C^k}<\infty$), exactly as this issue already proposes.
